cases.root_cause: The three pre-open option_snapshots failures on 2026-10-15 were one short transient IBKR Gateway/connectivity blip at about 09:10-09:20 ET, not a lasting outage. The 09:10 slot run lost the Gateway connection mid-request (SPX quote gone, then socket disconnect, then a connect TimeoutError in 4 s), so the pre-open runs for that slot failed and were lost (option snapshots can't be backfilled). Collection recovered on its own within the same window: the rest of the day's option and index snapshots succeeded (81 ok / 3 failed for options, 82 ok / 1 failed for indices) and the session's option coverage was 78/78 slots (100%), so no intervention was needed and none is called for.

Alpaca answered on 2026-10-15 but the intraday equity_bars response was short of bars for the symbol set: every intraday run that afternoon reported missing_bars=700 while rows grew from 2100 to 3200 (vs 3900 on full days), i.e. ~700 bars not returned by the vendor, not a collector or Gateway failure. No failed runs. The 17:30 eod refetch recovered them: SLI 3 reads 100% (3900/3900 bars) for session 2026-10-15, so no data is lost.

The 09:10:02 ET option_snapshots and index_snapshots runs are the only two failures of the day on the IBKR side, both dying in 4 s with a bare TimeoutError() — the signature of the Gateway's API port not accepting a connection. The Gateway was unusable at the open (the previous successful IBKR collection was ~62,101 s earlier, i.e. before the overnight gap), so both tasks timed out on connect rather than on quotes. Because the scheduled__2026-10-16T13:10:00 slot is the same pre-open/warm-up slot that in incidents/2026-10-26 preceded the Gateway freeze (secdef stall → wedged API port), the failure is consistent with a Gateway that was not accepting API connections at the start of the session rather than with an upstream data or vendor problem. The tool data alone does not show a reconnect/login code (1100/1102) or a secdef message at 09:10, so the specific trigger is not proven.

An IBKR 1100 (connectivity lost) event around 10:10 ET left one IBKR request hanging with no effective request timeout in a run on the option/index snapshot path; because that request never returned, the run stalled behind it and, with max_active_runs=1, every slot queued behind it started late. The stall was a scheduling/hang problem, not data loss: all 78 option slots for 2026-10-16 still succeeded, so the missing "new snapshots" between ~09:50 and 10:41 is late delivery of the queued slots, not skipped collection. The Gateway was not frozen and did not restart (runs continued to succeed before and after, and no restart/reconnect was needed).

A single equity_bars slot on 2026-10-16 at 10:09:43 ET failed after 18 s with an Alpaca RemoteProtocolError ('Server disconnected without sending a response.') — a vendor-side connection drop. It did not repeat: the next slots succeeded (rows counting up normally through the session) and the 17:30 eod refetch wrote 3900 bars with missing_bars=0 for 2026-10-05 through 2026-10-16, so the missed ~5-minute window was recovered and nothing was lost.

The 09:20:01 ET option_snapshots run failed after 480 s with no error recorded in pipeline_runs; nothing else on 2026-10-19 corroborates a Gateway fault (no failed index_snapshots or equity_bars runs, no 11xx/21xx codes on that run) and the day's option coverage is 78/78 (100%), so the data shown does not identify a specific cause. Whether it is a hung request or a run that exhausted its 8-min chains budget cannot be distinguished from these tools.

Codes 10090, 10167 and 354 are IBKR market-data permission codes, not a connectivity fault: 10090/354 mean the collector username is not subscribed for those instruments, and 10167 means IBKR returned delayed data instead of live. On 2026-10-19 they are reported on the alternating option_snapshot slots (roughly every third 5-minute slot), which collected on delayed quotes with elevated no_quote counts; the runs still succeeded and the session met all three SLIs. This is a Client Portal subscription gap on the collector user, so self-healing/reconnect cannot fix it. The separate 09:20:01 run failure (480 s duration) is a timeout, not a subscription error.

The 0% option coverage on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 is a monitoring artifact, not lost data: no pipeline_runs are recorded on this host for 10-22, 10-23 or 10-26, so the SLI counts zero option slots even though collected data exists. slo.md's "100% on 10-22" figure was computed on the Mac (9 sessions 2026-10-14 → 10-26) from the other machine's run records, whereas this host's pipeline_runs has no rows for those days and its SLI window instead includes pre-10-14 sessions (09-29 → 10-13 at 0%) that were never recorded here.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for ~5 minutes at 10:35 ET. Every option and index run first called qualifyContracts / reqSecDefOptParams (once per chain) before any quote request; with RequestTimeout = 300 s, one hung contract-definition request consumed the whole 6-min option run budget and blew the 2-min index task timeout. The lost 10:35 index slot is a consequence of that stall plus retries (max_active_runs=1), not of market data or the Gateway farms, which logged no errors and kept streaming quotes.

The 08:15:04 ET contract_cache refresh re-listed every cached expiry (~23.7 MB / 23,376 messages), overloading IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service; by 08:22:44 the market-data farm hfarm broke (2103) and secdef requests stopped answering. A hung qualifyContracts at 09:02 escaped check_gateway so self-healing never ran, and from 09:16 the Gateway's API port accepted no connections at all; IBC's RESTART could not fix it, so option snapshots were lost for the whole session until a container restart with 2FA login at 19:40:10 ET.

Yes — same cause as the documented morning secdef-stall pattern, but this time it was transient: the pre-open 09:10 runs' first contract-definition request hung until the ~2-min task timeout, killing the option and index runs. The Gateway recovered by itself — the next morning runs on 10-27 (11:50+ shown all ok) and every RTH slot on 10-30 completed normally (82 runs, 1 failed each day), and both days finished 78/78 option slots. This matches the recurring 08:15 contract_cache secdef overload described in incidents/2026-10-26 (recurring 10-28 → 11-02, fixed by ef762db), not the 10-23 stall (which hit 10:35 and late slots, not 09:10). The data confirms the symptom and pattern but not the secdef attribution directly, hence medium confidence; no action needed.

The 1100/2103 at ~10:00 were a transient IBKR connectivity loss plus a data-farm drop that recovered by themselves: 1102 at 10:05 restored the same session ("data maintained") and 2110 signalled the farm back. All 78 option slots on 2026-11-05 succeeded, so no data was lost and no action is needed.

Nothing is wrong with the Gateway. The 2157/2103 events are routine, self-recovering IBKR market-data farm blips: on both 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 the option_snapshots DAG had 82 runs with 0 failed and 0 failed morning runs, and per runbooks/gateway section D, a farm code that recovers within the same run (2103 then 2104, or 2157 followed by data) is routine and explicitly not alerted. Both days still met all three SLOs.

The four 09:10–09:25 option and index snapshot slots did not run late because of a slow Gateway: they never started on time, then failed together in a burst at 09:25:15–09:26:03 with TimeoutError() (and one "every chain failed: ConnectionError('Socket disconnect')"). The runs themselves fail in only 4–29 s, so IBKR's API was refusing/hanging on connect and dropping the socket when the queued slots were finally dispatched; the slots were subsequently recovered, since the session ends at 78/78 option slots (coverage 100%). The data does not identify which Gateway failure mode caused the ~75-minute pre-start stall (no run records cover 08:15–09:25 and there is no 1100/2157 code logged for this day), so this is not attributed to a specific cause.

The data volume filled up: from 13:05:00 ET on 2026-11-12 every collection run (all six datasets) fails within ~2 s with OSError(28, 'No space left on device'). The last good runs were the 13:00:00 ET slots; afterwards nothing can be written. The Gateway and IBKR are not involved (no IBKR error codes, no connection codes in any run).

The eod `dbt build` could not open `/opt/airflow/data/curated.duckdb` because another process held a lock on the file (conflicting lock held by /usr/local/bin/python3.12, PID 4127) — a stale or ad-hoc DuckDB session left open across 17:30 ET. Collection itself is unaffected: collectors write raw/staged Parquet, not through DuckDB. Find and close PID 4127, then re-run the build (or clear the dbt_build task so close_summary reruns).

Every equity_bars run today was rejected by Alpaca with HTTP 401 Unauthorized; the Alpaca API key/credentials used by the collector are invalid or revoked (or the account changed), so no bars were written. The IB Gateway/IBKR side is unaffected, which is why option and index snapshots (15:45 snapshot run, 10 index runs successful) kept working.

IBKR error 10197 on every option snapshot run: the collector user's live market data is held by another session of the same username (a TWS/mobile/web login), so requests succeed but return no quotes (two_sided/ask_only/bid_only all 0, no_quote 3400, ~170 flagged). Not a gateway wedge (runs still connect and finish in ~4-5 min) and not a subscription gap (otherwise 354/10089/10090 would appear).

Nothing ran on 2026-11-12: the whole stack (host, Docker or Airflow) was down, not the IB Gateway. 2026-11-11 closed cleanly (257 runs, 0 failed, last activity at 17:31:14 ET) and 2026-11-12 has zero recorded runs for every dataset, so no cards were sent either — the exact "no cards at all on a session day" signature in runbooks/stale-snapshots. There is no gateway/farm/frozen-port pattern (that would leave failed runs with TimeoutError or farm codes).

A contract-definition (secdef) stall at IB Gateway: contract-definition requests stopped answering (the 08:20 check card's ❌ 合约查询 timed out at 20 s), so the pre-open snapshot runs hung on their first secdef request until their execution timeout. The option runs burned their 6-min budget on spx_monthly's TimeoutError, so spx_weekly was skipped and every chain failed; index runs were killed by their 2-min timeout. Consistent with the 08:15 contract_cache refresh triggering the stall (per runbooks/gateway section B and incidents/2026-10-23); data returned without any Gateway restart, so it was not a wedged Gateway or a data-farm outage.

Six option_snapshot runs in the 11:00–11:30 ET window (11:00:00, 11:05, 11:10, 11:15, 11:20, 11:25:01 ET) hung after connecting to the Gateway and were killed at the run/request timeout (each exactly 480 s), which is why they show no error message — a hang, not an exception. Index snapshots (0 failed) and equity bars were unaffected, and the only IBKR code on the day was 2103, so this was not a persistent farm drop, subscription problem or host/vendor outage. The data does not identify which request stalled (no secdef/cache activity in that window), so the specific triggering request is unconfirmed.

IBKR market-data farms were disconnected (2103/2105) for the 13:00–13:25 ET window: option snapshot runs failed because SPX had no spot price. The collector's own RECONNECTDATA call returned OK and the farms recovered by themselves — the 13:30 ET option run succeeded and all runs through 15:55 ET were clean — so this was a transient farm disconnect, not a Gateway wedge or a subscription problem. Its only lasting effect is a coverage loss: 6 of 78 option slots missing on 2026-11-12 (SLI1 92.31%, below the 99% objective).

IB Gateway was down behind an unapproved 2FA login: 2FA was initiated at 08:58 and "Login has completed" did not appear until 10:17, so the API refused/hung every connect between ~09:08 and 10:17. Every option_snapshots and index_snapshots run in that window failed its connect with TimeoutError() after ~4 s. Nothing wedged and nothing secdef- or farm-related: once the login completed at 10:17, collection resumed on its own with no restart or RECONNECTDATA.

Alpaca answered every equity_bars run (no failed runs, no API errors), but the bars for roughly 12:45 on are missing from the vendor response (missing_bars=450 on each run); this is a vendor data gap, not a collection failure. Equity bars are refetchable, so the 17:30 ET eod runs that re-pull the last 10 sessions should recover them for intraday snapshots; session-level coverage still reads low until that is verified.

The 11:00 option_snapshots run hit a 1100 connectivity loss (immediately restored, 1102, same session — a routine blip, not a Gateway outage). A request in that run then hung with no short request timeout and only died at the 300 s RequestTimeout, raising TimeoutError() and failing the slot; because option snapshot tasks have max_active_runs=1 and no retries, the following slots started only when the previous run ended, so they ran ~4-5 min late from ~11:05 to ~11:30 until the schedule caught up. This is the 2026-10-23 pattern (hung request consuming the run budget after a connectivity loss), not a data-farm disconnect: codes were 1100/1102 only, the Gateway stayed connected, and index_snapshots had 0 failures today, so the API port was accepting connections.
